outcome.technical: tools/release.py: new run_finished(state) (every STEPS entry done; a no---push run's skipped remote steps are not finished) and set_aside_finished(state_path, state, version) -> (state, line). cmd_run calls it only when no --state was given: a finished run of ANOTHER version at the default .claude/state/release-run.json is moved with os.replace to release-run-<its version>.json beside it and the run starts from an empty state, printing one line ('the state file at X held release 3.5.0, finished (every step done) - kept as history at Y; this run starts fresh for 3.7.0'). Unfinished, same-version or unversioned state comes back unchanged and run_pipeline's existing version refusal decides; an archive name already taken, a version unfit for a file name or an OSError leaves the file in place and prints why before the refusal. Design choice: the default path is NOT keyed by version, because cmd_run's resume path reads the version back out of the default file when --version is omitted (rl6, rl7 bare `release.py --push`), so keying would break a resume typed without --version; setting the finished record aside keeps that path and loses no history. Module docstring gained a paragraph stating this. Cases added: rl26 (the acceptance), rl26b (record kept byte for byte at release-run-3.5.0.json; default now tracks 3.7.0), rl26c (second direction: a 3.5.0 prepared without --push still refuses, nothing run, nothing moved), rl26d (archive name taken: nothing overwritten, line names it, refusal stands).
